subject: Build the canonical Recall benchmark
description:
## What to build

Deliver the complete Batch 2 Recall benchmark foundation: one canonical suite, independent semantic scoring, one atomic Git baseline, full baseline comparison, deterministic validation, and live acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tracer slices 2.1 through 2.5 are complete in dependency order.
- [ ] The benchmark remains a black-box consumer of the public Recall CLI.
- [ ] Normal repository validation remains model-free and `bun run check` passes.
- [ ] The initial live baseline is human-reviewed and committed.

## Source

Derived from `specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-benchmark.md`: Summary, Goal, Completion Criteria, and Tracer-Bullet Implementation Slices.
context:
## Execution context

Coordinate the approved Batch 2 implementation without expanding production Recall behavior or inspecting private Recall internals for benchmark convenience.

## Relevant project context

- Primary package: `packages/agentic-memory-retrieval-bench/`.
- Public Recall decoding remains owned by `@urban/agentic-memory-core`.
- Follow `AGENTS.md`, including Effect v4 source verification and TypeScript import constraints.
- The roadmap already reflects the approved Batch 2 and Batch 12 boundary.

## Dependency context

- Child Tickets record the true implementation dependencies.

## Verification expectations

- Run `bun run check` before completion.

subject: Run the manifest-driven complete suite
description:
## What to build

Replace the hard-coded single-fixture orchestration with one manifest-driven, all-or-nothing canonical suite. Prepare `project-memory` and `user-preferences` once per run, assign all 16 migrated cases to exactly one fixture, and run them through a Recall-subject service with public-CLI and deterministic fake adapters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Strict suite, fixture, and case manifests reject invalid identities, path escapes, and incomplete assignments.
- [ ] Both disposable fixtures initialize and index through public Agentic Memory commands and clean up safely.
- [ ] All 16 existing case IDs and questions run in canonical order without filters or `--vault` override.
- [ ] The real subject invokes only the public Recall CLI; deterministic tests use a domain-shaped fake subject.
- [ ] Fixture preparation occurs exactly once per fixture and normal tests remain model-free.

## Source

Derived from Slice 2.1, Fixture Design, Corpus Migration, Recall-Subject Seam, and the corresponding Completion Criteria in `specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-benchmark.md`.

subject: Score responses with independent judgments
description:
## What to build

Replace required-substring quality scoring with authoritative reference answers, deterministic status and forbidden-fact precedence, and independent three-level semantic judgments through fake and isolated Pi subscription adapters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Answered and not-found expectations form a strict discriminated contract with reviewed reference answers.
- [ ] Status and forbidden-fact violations deterministically produce Incorrect and bypass the judge.
- [ ] Eligible answered responses are judged exactly once as Correct, Partially correct, or Incorrect with a bounded rationale and benchmark-owned score.
- [ ] The live adapter uses isolated `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol` with high reasoning, no tools or persisted context, strict schema decoding, fixed timeout, and no retries.
- [ ] Reports include equal-weight suite score and approved lean metrics; normal tests use fake adapters only.

## Source

Derived from Slice 2.2, Judgment Service, Scoring and Metrics, Failure Semantics, and Testing Strategy in `specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-benchmark.md`.
context:
## Execution context

Add scoring as benchmark-owned domain policy. The judge receives only the question, exhaustive reference answer, and public Recall response; it must not see fixtures, baseline answers, competing answers, or private Recall details.

## Relevant project context

- Replace `answerMustContain`; preserve explicit forbidden facts with the approved normalization rule.
- Process and decode failures are typed invalid-run failures, never Incorrect scores.
- Consult the installed Pi CLI documentation and exact command behavior before implementing the isolated adapter.
- Use Effect services and deterministic substitutes following repository rules.

## Dependency context

- Blocked by the manifest-driven suite because judgment consumes its complete case and subject contracts.

## Verification expectations

- Add contract, service, scoring, adapter-boundary, and report tests.
- Run the package check and `bun run check`; do not invoke live models in normal tests.

subject: Update the canonical baseline atomically
description:
## What to build

Add compatibility fingerprints, provenance, a strict canonical baseline artifact, and explicit atomic `--update` creation and replacement with equivalent human and JSON reports.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Corpus and judge SHA-256 fingerprints cover every approved compatibility input and reject mismatches before live work.
- [ ] Baselines strictly store the complete run, case inputs, public responses, evaluations, scores, metrics, and approved provenance.
- [ ] `--update` writes only after a complete operationally valid run and atomically replaces the canonical baseline.
- [ ] Every invalid-run failure point preserves any prior baseline byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Lower scores and deterministic quality failures remain eligible for an explicitly requested update, with hard gates reported visibly.
- [ ] Human and JSON update reports contain the same substantive evidence.

## Source

Derived from Slice 2.3, Compatibility and Provenance, Baseline Policy, Failure Semantics, Reports, and CLI Behavior in `specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-benchmark.md`.
context:
## Execution context

Implement one canonical generated baseline under `packages/agentic-memory-retrieval-bench/baselines/`. Git is artifact history; do not add an artifact schema-version or migration framework.

## Relevant project context

- Fingerprints must use a canonical representation independent of temporary paths, timestamps, Git state, generated indexes, and model output.
- Record Git revision and dirty state plus judge/Pi provenance without credentials.
- Filesystem replacement and cleanup must use scoped, failure-safe Effect patterns.

## Dependency context

- Blocked by independent judgments because the baseline persists complete evaluated runs and judge compatibility.

## Verification expectations

- Test atomic creation/replacement, preservation across every invalid stage, mismatch rejection, provenance safety, and report parity.
- Run the package check and `bun run check`.

subject: Compare complete runs against the baseline
description:
## What to build

Make the default complete benchmark run require a compatible canonical baseline, reuse its stored judgments, judge only new eligible answers, and report every baseline-versus-new case and aggregate delta.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing, undecodable, corpus-incompatible, or judge-incompatible baselines fail before live work with `--update` guidance.
- [ ] Baseline answers and judgments are reused exactly and never recomputed during comparison.
- [ ] Every new eligible answer is judged exactly once; deterministic cases bypass the judge.
- [ ] Human and JSON reports show every case, reference answer, baseline and new answer/evaluation/rationale, score delta, hard gates, revisions, metrics, and advisory durations.
- [ ] Pure judge-score regressions remain advisory while status and forbidden-fact violations retain nonzero exit behavior.
- [ ] Normal comparisons never mutate the baseline.

## Source

Derived from Slice 2.4, User Workflow, Comparison Report, Reports, CLI Behavior, and Exit Behavior in `specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-benchmark.md`.
context:

## Relevant project context

- JSON stdout must be exactly one schema-validated discriminated result; diagnostics go to stderr.

## Verification expectations

- Run the package check and `bun run check`.

subject: Finalize regression workflow and acceptance
description:
## What to build

Finish the Batch 2 implementation by documenting the failure-to-regression workflow, enforcing actionable typed invalid-run behavior, removing obsolete benchmark options and substring expectations, and proving the complete deterministic suite is live-ready.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--vault`, filters, selectors, tags, and obsolete required-substring behavior are removed and rejected with usage guidance.
- [ ] Recall and judge timeouts terminate and settle children, close resources, clean temporary vaults, and preserve the baseline.
- [ ] Human and JSON invalid-run and invalid-argument boundaries match the approved contracts and exit codes.
- [ ] README and roadmap documentation describe the canonical update, comparison, and failure-to-regression workflows accurately.
- [ ] Deterministic contract, service, baseline, CLI, report, and process-adapter tests cover the PRD requirements without models or network access.
- [ ] The package is ready for the opt-in live proof and `bun run check` passes.

## Source

Derived from Slice 2.5, Failure-to-Regression Workflow, Failure Semantics, Testing Strategy, CLI Behavior, and Completion Criteria in `specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-benchmark.md`.

subject: Approve the initial live benchmark baseline
description:
## What to build

Perform the required opt-in live proof, review the generated canonical baseline as a Git snapshot, and approve the initial committed baseline for Batch 2 completion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The local synthesis server, embedding model, Pi subscription authentication, exact judge provider/model, and high reasoning configuration are available.
- [ ] A complete `--update` run prepares both fixtures, recalls all 16 cases, judges every eligible answer, and finishes without operational failure.
- [ ] The generated baseline and complete report are reviewed for reference-answer fidelity, forbidden facts, judgments, provenance safety, scores, and hard-gate visibility.
- [ ] The reviewed baseline is committed together with any required corpus state.
- [ ] No credentials, bearer tokens, private memory, or generated semantic indexes are committed.

## Source

Derived from Live Proof, Baseline Policy, Completion Criteria, and the PRD's Git-diff approval mechanism in `specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-benchmark.md`.
context:
## Execution context

This is a human-owned gate. A person must provide or confirm access to the local Qwen synthesis runtime and existing ChatGPT subscription, run or supervise the live benchmark, review the generated baseline diff, and decide whether to commit it. Do not execute this Ticket unattended.

## Relevant project context

- Command: `bun --filter='./packages/agentic-memory-retrieval-bench' run bench -- --update`.
- Required judge: `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol` with high reasoning through isolated Pi.
- The update may legitimately record Incorrect cases; the baseline records observed behavior while reference answers remain desired truth.

## Dependency context

- Blocked by final regression workflow and deterministic acceptance because the live proof must exercise the completed implementation.
- Completion unblocks closing the benchmark epic and beginning benchmark-gated Recall ranking work.

## Verification expectations

- Review the complete human or JSON report and Git diff.
- Run `bun run check` after the committed baseline is present.
